Otherwise the translator fails with the reason and the line, for example `The fragment is not complete: it ends before its closing (line 2)`. Goldens for every language are in `examples/programs/fragments/translated/` and are checked by `write-fragments.mjs --check`.\\n\\n### CLI, library, HTTP API and Docker\\n\\n- `universal-translator serve` starts an HTTP API (`GET /languages`, `POST /translate`). It reads `--port`/`--host`, then `PORT`/`HOST`, then `.lenv`, through lino-arguments.\\n- `js/src/index.js` (with types) and the `rust/` crate are the libraries.\\n- The `Dockerfile` image runs the CLI and the server. The release workflow builds it and smoke tests the CLI and the HTTP API.\\n\\n### Source layout and best practices\\n\\n- Sources are split into `src/meta` (shared types and trees), `src/formal` (programming languages, Lean, Rocq and machine code) and `src/natural` (human languages, with a reader and a writer), in both `js/` and `rust/`. The `source-layout` check rejects imports that point outwards from the meta layer.\\n- [`docs/case-studies/issue-1/best-practices.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/universal-translator/blob/issue-1-35d65b774bf6/docs/case-studies/issue-1/best-practices.md) maps the associative technology stack, the code architecture principles and all 17 CI/CD best practices to evidence, or gives a reason when one does not apply. `cargo clippy -D warnings` now runs in CI.\\n- **Test coverage is required by CI.** `npm run test:coverage` replaces `npm test` in the Node.js job. It fails below 94% line, 91% branch or 95% function coverage of `js/src` and `bin`; current coverage is 95.4%, 92.1% and 96.5%. The Rust crate runs the same goldens, but CI does not measure its coverage.\\n\\n### Programming languages (32) and machine code\\n\\n| | |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| Languages | JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Lua, PHP, C, C++, C#, Java, Go, Rust, Kotlin, Swift, Perl, Dart, Scala, Julia, R, Groovy, Objective-C, Nim, D, Pascal, Fortran, Ada, Visual Basic .NET, Bash, MATLAB/Octave, Zig, **Lean 4, Rocq** |\\n| Dialects | Pascal, Fortran, Ada, VB.NET, Bash, MATLAB/Octave and Zig have their own program layout. They are dialects of the shared parser and emitter (`js/src/formal/dialects/`, `rust/src/formal/dialects/`). Lean 4 programs use `partial def` and `IO`. Rocq programs are pure `Fixpoint`s over an output monad defined in a small runtime, and are evaluated with `Eval vm_compute`. |\\n| Machine targets | NASM, CIL and JVM are written through a named stack machine and read back by lifting, so machine code translates to every language and between targets. |\\n| Modes | context-dependent (default, adapts comments such as C \\\"function call\\\" → C# \\\"method call\\\"), literal, same-effect |\\n| Extensibility | Every stage and rule list is an option of `createGrammarTranslator`; custom meta → meta layers are supported. |\\n| Common library | `common-library/` (output operations only, one file per language), enabled with `--common-library` |\\n\\n### Controlled natural languages\\n\\n- Data lives in `data/natural/*.lino`; `js/src/natural/` and `rust/src/natural/` read and write the same texts byte for byte.\\n- Covers the 30 most spoken languages (English, Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, French, Arabic, Bengali, Portuguese, Russian, Urdu, Indonesian, German, Japanese, Marathi, Telugu, Turkish, Tamil, Vietnamese, Korean, Italian, Persian, Swahili, Tagalog, Thai, Polish, Ukrainian, Hausa, Gujarati, Punjabi, Dutch), each in a small controlled form (`cnl-default`).\\n- Profiles for the standards named in the issue:\\n  - ASD-STE100\\n  - Attempto Controlled English\\n  - Gellish (English and Dutch)\\n  - SBVR Structured English\\n  - Plain language (ISO 24495-1)\\n  - E-Prime\\n  - Basic English, VOA Special English and Globish\\n  - Minimal English, Minimal French and Minimal Polish, built on the **65 semantic primes** of NSM (`data/natural/semantic-primes.lino`)\\n- `checkText` and the `check-words` command enforce each standard's rules: sentence length, allowed first words, forbidden words such as \\\"to be\\\" in E-Prime or \\\"shall\\\" in plain language, vocabulary limits, and Gellish relation phrases.\\n- Translations run natural → meta → any programming or machine language, and back: `universal-translator translate russian python`, `translate python spanish`.\\n- Every example program is written in every natural language and profile under `examples/programs/natural/`. Each text is read back to the same meaning and checked against its standard.\\n\\n### Rosetta Code and Hello World\\n\\n18 tasks in `examples/programs/` are translated to all 32 languages, the 3 machine targets and every natural language, then run natively:\\n\\n- hello world\\n- factorial\\n- greatest common divisor\\n- FizzBuzz\\n- sum of squares\\n- Fibonacci\\n- Ackermann\\n- Towers of Hanoi\\n- leap year\\n- sum of digits\\n- hailstone\\n- 99 bottles\\n- primality by trial division\\n- mutual recursion\\n- perfect numbers\\n- sieve of Eratosthenes\\n- bubble sort\\n- sum and product of an array\\n\\nAlgorithm types covered (from `rosetta-coverage.lino`): output, integer arithmetic, conditionals, iteration, functions, recursion (including mutual recursion), number theory, text concatenation, and **integer arrays** (new: array values in the meta language, all 32 languages, NASM/CIL/JVM and natural-language sentences).\\n\\n**Blocked, with reasons recorded in `rosetta-coverage.lino`.** These are not presented as done. Rosetta Code has more than 1,300 tasks, and these types need values the meta language does not have yet:\\n\\n| Type | Why it is blocked |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| floating-point | Machine targets and the meta language use 64-bit integers only |\\n| string manipulation | Text can be printed and concatenated, but not indexed or transformed |\\n| higher-order functions | Functions are top-level declarations only |\\n| data structures | Records, maps, stacks and queues need compound values |\\n| input/output | Programs only write to standard output, which is what the native checks compare |\\n| objects and concurrency | Not supported |\\n\\n**Classes as fragments** are also **blocked** (`class-fragments` in the gate) for the same reason: the meta language has no objects or classes, so a class has no meaning to translate yet.\\n\\nThe gate reports `rosetta-algorithm-types` and `class-fragments` as **BLOCKED** with these reasons. Every other requirement is **DONE**.\\n\\n## Verification\\n\\n- **`npm test` (Node, Bun, Deno) and `cargo test`.** Every task is translated to every language, machine target and natural language and compared with the goldens in `examples/programs/translated` and `examples/programs/natural`.\\n- **`examples/programs/verify-native.mjs --require-all [--common-library]`.** The `native-translation` CI job compiles or runs each translation with its real toolchain and compares the output with the JavaScript original. The toolchains include Lean 4 (elan), Rocq (opam), fpc, gnat, gfortran, octave, zig, nim, ldc, Objective-C, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, .NET and Jasmin.\\n- **`experiments/verify-syntax-exchange.sh`.** The JS and Rust command lines list the same 32 languages and write identical output.\\n- **`node scripts/check-requirements.mjs`.** The requirements gate described above.\\n- **`npm run test:coverage`.** The coverage gate described above.\\n- **`web-e2e`.** The browser test of the demo.\\n- **`--trace`.** Logs each pipeline stage.\\n\\n### CI reliability (native translation job)\\n\\n- Toolchain archives are cached. Each download attempt is capped at 3 minutes and falls back to a mirror: Google's Maven Central mirror for Groovy and `zig.linus.dev` for Zig, all checked by SHA-256. This fixes a run where the step hung on a stalled download.\\n- `verify-native.mjs` runs its checks in parallel worker processes.\\n- `js/tests/ci-timeouts.test.js` keeps each job's step budgets within 70% of its backstop.\\n- Budgets are sized for slower runners. One run needed 330 s for all native translations and over 360 s for the common library translations, while a typical run needs about 220 s and 250 s. Every translation passed, but the 360 s budget ran out. The step budgets are now 540 s and 480 s, and the job backstop is 100 minutes so the budgets stay within 70% of it.\\n\\n### CodeQL\\n\\n- `js/incomplete-sanitization` flagged the Lean `s!\\\"…\\\"` brace escape, because it was chained after `escape()` where CodeQL cannot see that backslashes were already escaped. All-or-nothing\n// translation throws the whole text away for that one part. Partial\n// translation keeps everything it can read and marks the rest.\n//\n// The text is cut into parts along its own layout, so the method needs no\n// grammar of its own and works for every language:\n//\n// 1. A part starts at a line and may end before any later line that is\n//    indented no deeper than its first line, unless that line only closes\n//    or continues the part (`}`, `end`, `else`, ...).\n// 2. The first form is the one a translation writes; the other\n// forms (cases, plurals, tenses) are read.\n//\n// The grammar of a language states:\n//\n//   infinitive  how an infinitive is written around the verb ('to {verb}')\n//   verb-lemma  'infinitive' when the first form of a verb is its infinitive\n//   endings     inflection endings, so an inflected form that is not listed\n//               is still found through its stem (мира -> мир)\n//   spaced      'no' when words are written without spaces between them\n\nimport { parseLinks } from '../meta/links.js';\nimport { naturalSources } from './sources.js';\n\nconst fold = (text) => text.toLocaleLowerCase();\nconst length = (text) => [...text].length;\n\nlet concepts;\n\n// [{ id, part, forms: { language: [form, ...] } }] in the order of the file,\n// the most frequent concept first.\nexport function vocabularyConcepts() {\n  if (!concepts) {\n    const [root] = parseLinks(naturalSources['vocabulary.lino']);\n    concepts = root.values.map(({ id, values }) => {\n      const forms = {};\n      let part;\n      for (const field of values) {\n        const words = field.values.map((value) => value.id);\n        if (field.id === 'part') {\n          [part] = words;\n        } else {\n          forms[field.id] = words.map(fold);\n        }\n      }\n      return { id, part, forms };\n    });\n  }\n  return concepts;\n}\n\nlet grammars;\n\n// The grammar of a base language (every field is optional).\nexport function grammarOf(base) {\n  if (!grammars) {\n    const [root] = parseLinks(naturalSources['grammar.lino']);\n    grammars = new Map(\n      root.values.map(({ id, values }) => {\n        const fields = Object.fromEntries(\n          values.map((field) => [\n            field.id,\n            field.values.map((value) => value.id),\n          ])\n        );\n        // Longer endings first, so the shortest stem is tried last.\n        const endings = (fields.endings ??     "originalFile": "// Comment language: translate only the comments of a program, word by word,\n// with the dictionaries the natural languages already have.\n//\n// A comment dictionary pairs the phrases of two natural languages through\n// their shared meaning: the neutral words of program names (the `words` of\n// each language description) and the exponents of the semantic primes. The\n// longest known phrase wins; unknown words, numbers, punctuation and every\n// space stay as they are, so the layout inside a comment is kept.\n//\n// A dictionary cannot translate free prose well. Callers with a better\n// translator (a machine translation service, a human) pass it as\n// `translateComment(text, { from, to })`; the dictionary is the default.\n\nimport { naturalLanguage, naturalLanguageIds } from './catalog.js';\nimport { semanticPrimes } from './rules.js';\n\nconst fold = (text) => text.toLocaleLowerCase();\nconst baseOf = (id) => naturalLanguage(id).base ?? id;\n\nlet neutral;\n// Every neutral word some language has a word for.\nfunction neutralWords() {\n  neutral ??= [\n    ...new Set(\n      naturalLanguageIds().flatMap((id) =>\n        Object.keys(naturalLanguage(id).lexicon)\n      )\n    ),\n  ];\n  return neutral;\n}\n\n// Neutral meaning -> phrases of one language, the preferred phrase first.\nfunction phrasesOf(id) {\n  const language = naturalLanguage(id);\n  const base = baseOf(id);\n  const phrases = new Map();\n  const add = (meaning, phrase) => {\n    if (!phrase) {\n      return;\n    }\n    const known = phrases.get(meaning) ?? [];\n    if (!known.includes(fold(phrase))) {\n      phrases.set(meaning, [...known, fold(phrase)]);\n    }\n  };\n  for (const { prime, exponents } of semanticPrimes()) {\n    (exponents[base] ?? []).forEach((phrase) => add(`prime:${prime}`, phrase));\n  }\n  // Program words are neutral English words: English spells each of them as\n  // it is (or in its regional spelling, color -> colour), other languages\n  // through their lexicon.\n  if (base === 'english') {\n    for (const neutral of neutralWords()) {\n      add(`word:${neutral}`, language.lexicon[neutral]);\n      add(`word:${neutral}`, neutral);\n    }\n  } else {\n    for (const [neutral, word] of Object.entries(language.lexicon)) {\n      add(`word:${neutral}`, word);\n    }\n  }\n  return phrases;\n}\n\nconst dictionaries = new Map();\n\n// Phrase of `from` -> phrase of `to`, for every meaning both languages have.\nexport function commentDictionary(from, to) {\n  const key = `${from}>${to}`;\n  // A standard registered again under the same id is a new language object.\n  const languages = [naturalLanguage(from), naturalLanguage(to)];\n  const known = dictionaries.get(key);\n  if (known?.languages.every((language, at) => language === languages[at])) {\n    return known.dictionary;\n  }\n  const source = phrasesOf(from);\n  const target = phrasesOf(to);\n  const dictionary = new Map();\n  for (const [meaning, phrases] of source) {\n    const [preferred] = target.get(meaning) ?? Phrases of up to\n// four words joined by single spaces are tried longest first.\nexport function translateCommentText(text, { from, to }) {\n  if (baseOf(from) === baseOf(to) && from === to) {\n    return text;\n  }\n  const dictionary = commentDictionary(from, to);\n  const parts = pieces(text);\n  let output = '';\n  let index = 0;\n  while (index < parts.length) {\n    if (index % 2 === 0) {\n      output += parts[index];\n      index += 1;\n      continue;\n    }\n    let matched = false;\n    for (let size = longestPhrase; size >= 1 && !matched; size -= 1) {\n      const end = index + 2 * (size - 1);\n      if (end >= parts.length) {\n        continue;\n      }\n      const gaps = parts.slice(index + 1, end).filter((_, at) => at % 2 === 0);\n      if (gaps.some((gap) => gap !== ' ')) {\n        continue;\n      }\n      const phrase = parts.slice(index, end + 1).join('');\n      const translated = dictionary.get(fold(phrase));\n      if (translated) {\n        output += matchCase(phrase, translated);\n        index = end + 1;\n        matched = true;\n      }\n    }\n    if (!matched) {\n      output += parts[index];\n      index += 1;\n    }\n  }\n  return output;\n}\n\nconst phraseSets = new WeakMap();\nfunction knownWords(id) {\n  const language = naturalLanguage(id);\n  if (!phraseSets.has(language)) {\n    phraseSets.set(\n      language,\n      new Set(\n        [...phrasesOf(id).values()]\n          .flat()\n          .flatMap((phrase) => phrase.split(' '))\n      )\n    );\n  }\n  return phraseSets.get(language);\n}\n\n// The natural language most words of the comments belong to (English when\n// no language knows them).\nexport function detectCommentLanguage(texts) {\n  const words = texts\n    .flatMap((text) => pieces(text).filter((_, index) => index % 2))\n    .map(fold);\n  let best = { id: 'english', score: 0 };\n  for (const id of naturalLanguageIds()) {\n    if (naturalLanguage(id).base) {\n      continue;\n    }\n    const known = knownWords(id);\n    const score = words.filter((word) => known.has(word)).length;\n    if (score > best.score) {\n      best = { id, score };\n    }\n  }\n  return best.id;\n}\n",

It must also skip 'vocabulary.lino' and 'grammar.lino', and Rust must do the same.\n   - Comment translation (js/src/natural/comments.js, mirrored in rust/src/natural/comments.rs):\n     - phrasesOf(id) maps meaning → phrases. Meanings are `prime:X` (exponents of the base language) and `word:X` (lexicon).\n     - commentDictionary(from, to) maps phrase → the preferred target phrase. It is exported from index.js.\n     - pieces() splits text with the regex `/([\\p{L}\\p{M}]+(?:['’-][\\p{L}\\p{M}]+)*)/u`.\n     - Phrases of up to 4 words are matched, longest first, with matchCase.\n     - knownWords and detectCommentLanguage choose among base languages and default to english.\n     - Used by js/src/translation/comment-language.js.\n   - Detection (detect.js):\n     - natural languages score by wordEvidence = 10 × known/words, where known = reserved ∪ reverseLexicon;\n     - profiles get -0.5;\n     - `reads` comes from parseFragment, and `coverage` comes from parsePartial for the best unread candidates;\n     - score = 100·coverage + evidence, and results with score ≤ 0 are filtered out.\n     - \"Hello world\" currently detects as ruby/perl/nim with coverage 1.\n   - Partial translation: createPartialTranslator({parseFragment, translateFragment, writeNotes}) writes a failed part as \"untranslated (line N): message\" plus the original lines as notes.\n   - Natural reader: ProgramReader.statement fails with 'No sentence template matches'. Notes ↔ Comment nodes.\n\n   Design decided for R9, R11–R14:\n   - **Vocabulary.** data/natural/vocabulary.lino holds concepts with `part:` and per-language forms. The first form is the lemma and the one that is written.\n   - **Grammar.** data/natural/grammar.lino holds per-language `infinitive` (english 'to {verb}'), `verb-lemma: infinitive`, `endings` (stemming with a minimum stem of 3 characters) and `spaced: no` (chinese, japanese, thai).\n   - **Meaning order.** For each language, meanings are primes, then lexicon words, then vocabulary concepts (`concept:X`). Parts are 'prime', 'name', or the concept's part.\n   - **Interrogatives.** Interrogative concepts are preferred inside questions only. A sentence is a question if the first terminator after the word is `?`, `？` or `؟`; terminators are `.!?;。！？؟`. Computed by walking the pieces right to left. Elsewhere interrogatives are a last resort.\n   - **Round trip.** The target phrase is the first target form whose own likeliest meaning (in the same question context) is the same meaning; otherwise the first form.\n   - **Articles.** An article with no target phrase is dropped together with the following single-space gap. If the article was capitalised, the next word is capitalised.\n   - **Infinitives.**\n     - A source verb is an infinitive when its first form matches exactly and the source grammar's verbLemma is 'infinitive', or when the source's infinitive pattern matches ('to' followed by a verb).\n     - The target writes its infinitive pattern around the verb.\n   - **Stemming fallback** goes through knownForm().\n   - **Unspaced text.**\n     - An unspaced source run is segmented greedily (up to 8 characters).\n     - Translated segments are joined with ' ' when the target is spaced.\n     - An unspaced target drops single-space gaps between translated words.\n   - **Free prose in partial translation.** createPartialTranslator gets a `translateProse` option. When from and to are both natural, failed parts are translated freely. They are marked `status: 'free'`/prose rather than as errors, and the result gains a `prose` list of line ranges. translate() (all-or-nothing) stays strict. Rust mirrors this (`PartialTranslation` gains a field).\n   - **Detection.**\n     - wordEvidence uses the known words of the vocabulary, primes and stems.\n     - Natural candidates get coverage = max(partial coverage, prose coverage), where prose coverage = known words / (words + count of code symbols `[{}()\\[\\];=<>+*/\\\\$#@&|^~\\``]`).\n     - Base languages beat profiles because of the -0.5.\n   - **Phrase entries** such as 'how-good' (как хорошо ↔ how good), so «Как хорошо покакать?» becomes \"How good to poop?\" and round-trips.\n\n3. A translator of one's own may know more.\nfunction checkCommentLanguages({\n  commentLanguage,\n  commentFrom,\n  translateComment,\n}) {\n  if (translateComment) {\n    return;\n  }\n  for (const id of [commentLanguage, commentFrom]) {\n    if (id) {\n      naturalLanguage(id);\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nfunction checkTarget(to, mode, commonLibrary) {\n  if (!modes.includes(mode)) {\n    throw new Error(`Unsupported mode \"${mode}\"`);\n  }\n  if (commonLibrary && machineTargetIds.includes(to)) {\n    throw new Error(`Machine targets have no common library (${to})`);\n  }\n  const natural = isNaturalLanguage(to);\n  if (natural && commonLibrary) {\n    throw new Error(`Natural languages have no common library (${to})`);\n  }\n  if (!natural) {\n    languageSyntax(to);\n  }\n}\n\n// Machine code is read and written as whole programs only.\nconst involvesMachineCode = (from, to) =>\n  machineTargetIds.includes(to) ||\n  (!isNaturalLanguage(from) && languageSyntax(from).machine);\n\n// The result of partial translation for a text translated as a whole.\nfunction completeResult(text, source) {\n  const lines = source.split('\\n').filter((line) => line.trim()).length;\n  return {\n    text,\n    complete: true,\n    errors: [],\n    lines,\n    readLines: lines,\n    coverage: 1,\n    prose: [],\n  };\n}\n\n// Two programming languages share a layout: the target keeps the spaces and\n// the blank lines around the code of the source (layout 'source', the\n// default) or is written as its emitter lays it out (layout 'target'). Both\n// map the lines of the target to the lines of the source.\n  return translateText(text, { from, to });\n}\n\n// Partial translation (the default of the command line, the server and the\n// web demo) keeps every part it can translate and marks the rest;\n// all-or-nothing translation throws at the first part it cannot read.\nfunction partialTranslator(translate, fragments, partial) {\n  function readAll(source, from, to, options) {\n    const whole = options.fragment ? fragments.translateFragment : translate;\n    try {\n      return completeResult(whole(source, from, to, options), source);\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (involvesMachineCode(from, to)) {\n        throw error;\n      }\n      return partial.translatePartial(source, from, to, options);\n    }\n  }\n  return (source, from, to, options = {}) => {\n    checkCommentLanguages(options);\n    if (options.layout !== undefined && !layouts.includes(options.layout)) {\n      throw new Error(`Unsupported layout \"${options.layout}\"`);\n    }\n    const result = readAll(source, from, to, options);\n    return withLayout(result, source, from, to, options);\n  };\n}\n\nexport function createGrammarTranslator(settings = {}) {\n  const {\n    parse = parseProgram,\n    understanding = understandingRules,\n    infer = inferTypes,\n    meaning = meaningRules,\n    context = contextRules,\n    layers = [],\n    emit = emitProgram,\n    emitMachineCode = emitMachine,\n    lift = liftProgram,\n    trace = () => {},\n    rules = {},\n  } = settings;\n  // Rules given as data (see translation/custom-rules.js).\n  const custom = compileCustomRules(rules);\n  const metaLayers = [...layers, ...custom.layers];\n\n  function toMeta(text, from) {\n    const source = custom.source(text, from);\n    if (isNaturalLanguage(from)) {\n      // A controlled natural language is read sentence by sentence straight\n      // into the meta language; it has no source details to understand.\n      const read = inferMutability(\n        readNatural(source, from, custom.naturalLanguage(from))\n      );\n      trace('read', read);\n      const typed = applyRules(infer(read), meaning, {});\n      trace('typed', typed);\n      return typed;\n    }\n    const syntax = languageSyntax(from);\n    if (syntax.machine) {\n      // Machine code has no grammar to parse: read its instructions, lift\n      // them to the meta language and continue like any other source.\n      const lifted = inferMutability(lift(readMachine(source, from)));\n      trace('lifted', lifted);\n      const typed = applyRules(infer(lifted), meaning, { from });\n      trace('typed', typed);\n      return typed;\n    }\n    const sourceTree = parse(source, syntax);\n    trace('parsed', sourceTree);\n    const meta = applyRules(sourceTree, understanding, { from });\n    trace('understood', meta);\n    const typed = applyRules(infer(meta), meaning, { from });\n    trace('typed', typed);\n    return typed;\n  }\n\n  // Run the custom layers and the context rules for a target. A natural\n  // target receives the transformed program, since it has no syntax to\n  // adapt to.\n  function adapt(meta, to, options = {}) {\n    const {\n      from = to,\n      mode = 'context-dependent',\n      commonLibrary = false,\n    } = options;\n    checkTarget(to, mode, commonLibrary);\n    const natural = isNaturalLanguage(to);\n    // Words carry no syntax of their own, so a program read from words is\n    // adapted as if it had been written in the target language.\n    // The rules adapt to the language; only writing depends on its version.\n    const settings = {\n      from: splitVersion(isNaturalLanguage(from) ? to : from).id,\n      to: splitVersion(to).id,\n      mode,\n    };\n    // Custom layers are meta -> meta transformations, so they see the target\n    // independent program; context rules then adapt it to the target.\n    // The common library route is one more meta layer, run last.\n    const allLayers = commonLibrary\n      ? [...metaLayers, [useCommonLibrary]]\n      : metaLayers;\n    const transformed = allLayers.reduce(\n      (current, layer) => applyRules(current, layer, settings),\n      meta\n    );\n    trace('transformed', transformed);\n    if (natural) {\n      return inCommentLanguage(transformed, options);\n    }\n    const adapted = applyRules(transformed, context, settings);\n    trace('adapted', adapted);\n    return inCommentLanguage(adapted, options);\n  }\n\n  function translate(source, from, to, options = {}) {\n    const { commentLanguage, commentFrom, translateComment } = options;\n    // Same code, other comment language: change only the comments, in place,\n    // so every character of the code stays.\n    if (\n      commentLanguage &&\n      from === to &&\n      !isNaturalLanguage(from) &&\n      !languageSyntax(from).machine\n    ) {\n      return translateComments(source, from, {\n        from: commentFrom,\n        to: commentLanguage,\n        translateComment,\n      });\n    }\n    return fromMeta(toMeta(source, from), to, { ...options, from });\n  }\n\n  // Write an adapted program in a language, a machine target or words.\n  const write = (adapted, to) => custom.output(writeTarget(adapted, to), to);\n  const emitText = (adapted, to) => custom.output(emit(adapted, to), to);\n\n  function writeTarget(adapted, to) {\n    if (isNaturalLanguage(to)) {\n      return writeNatural(adapted, to);\n    }\n    return machineTargetIds.includes(to)\n      ? emitMachineCode(adapted, to)\n      : emit(adapted, to);\n  }\n\n  function fromMeta(meta, to, options = {}) {\n    return write(adapt(meta, to, options), to);\n  }",

From it a link between both texts gives:\n//\n// - groups: lines that belong together (a statement written on three lines\n//   on one side and on one on the other), each with a colour of a cycling\n//   palette, so both editors show what translates to what;\n// - ranges: the lines on the other side of a selection;\n// - positions: where to scroll the other editor to. Lines matched exactly\n//   are anchors; between two anchors a position moves in proportion, so a\n//   part that takes ten lines on one side and two on the other scrolls\n//   both editors through it at once, as diff tools do.\n//\n// Nothing here needs Monaco or React: editor-sync.js applies it to the\n// editors. A side is 0 (the source) or 1 (the target).\n\nexport const paletteSize = 6;\n\n// Connected pairs: a line on either side joins every pair it is part of.\nfunction components(pairs) {\n  const parent = new Map();\n  const find = (key) => {\n    let root = key;\n    while (parent.get(root) !== root) {\n      root = parent.get(root);\n    }\n    parent.set(key, root);\n    return root;\n  };\n  const join = (a, b) => {\n    for (const key of [a, b]) {\n      if (!parent.has(key)) {\n        parent.set(key, key);\n      }\n    }\n    parent.set(find(a), find(b));\n  };\n  for (const [source, target] of pairs) {\n    join(`s${source}`, `t${target}`);\n  }\n  const groups = new Map();\n  for (const [source, target] of pairs) {\n    const root = find(`s${source}`);\n    if (!groups.has(root)) {\n      groups.set(root, [new Set(), new Set()]);\n    }\n    groups.get(root)[0].add(source);\n    groups.get(root)[1].add(target);\n  }\n  return [...groups.values()].map((sides) =>\n    sides.map((lines) => [...lines].sort((a, b) => a - b))\n  );\n}\n\n// The longest chain of pairs that goes down on both sides at once: the\n// anchors of scrolling (a pair that crosses another is left out).\nfunction monotonicChain(pairs) {\n  const sorted = [...pairs].sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0] || b[1] - a[1]);\n  const tails = [];\n  const previous = [];\n  sorted.forEach(([, target], index) => {\n    let low = 0;\n    let high = tails.length;\n    while (low < high) {\n      const middle = (low + high) >> 1;\n      if (sorted[tails[middle]][1] < target) {\n        low = middle + 1;\n      } else {\n        high = middle;\n      }\n    }\n    previous[index] = low > 0 ? tails[low - 1] : -1;\n    tails[low] = index;\n  });\n  const chain = [];\n  for (let at = tails.at(-1) ?? -1; at >= 0; at = previous[at]) {\n    chain.unshift(sorted[at]);\n  }\n  // One anchor per source line: the first of equal ones.\n  return chain.filter((pair, index) => chain[index - 1]?.[0] !== pair[0]);\n}\n\n// Anchors from the start to the end of both texts.\nfunction anchorsOf(pairs, counts) {\n  const chain = monotonicChain(pairs);\n  const first = chain[0];\n  if (!first || (first[0] > 0 && first[1] > 0)) {\n    chain.unshift([0, 0]);\n  }\n  const last = chain.at(-1);\n  if (counts[0] > last[0] && counts[1] > last[1]) {\n    chain.push([counts[0], counts[1]]);\n  }\n  return chain;\n}\n\n// A position (a line number with a fraction: 2.5 is half way through the\n// third line) on one side, as a position on the other side.\nexport function mapPosition(anchors, position, side = 0) {\n  const other = 1 - side;\n  if (anchors.length === 0) {\n    return position;\n  }\n  let at = -1;\n  while (at + 1 < anchors.length && anchors[at + 1][side] <= position) {\n    at += 1;\n  }\n  if (at < 0) {\n    return Math.max(0, anchors[0][other] - (anchors[0][side] - position));\n  }\n  const [from, to] = [anchors[at], anchors[at + 1]];\n  if (!to) {\n    return from[other] + (position - from[side]);\n  }\n  const ratio = (position - from[side]) / (to[side] - from[side]);\n  return from[other] + ratio * (to[other] - from[other]);\n}\n\n// A link between the lines of two texts. `counts` are their line counts.\nexport function lineLink(lineMap = [], counts = [0, 0]) {\n  const pairs = (lineMap ?? []).filter(\n    (pair) => Array.isArray(pair) && pair.length === 2\n  );\n  const groups = components(pairs)\n    .sort((a, b) => a[0][0] - b[0][0] || a[1][0] - b[1][0])\n    .map((lines, index) => ({ index, colour: index % paletteSize, lines }));\n  const byLine = [new Map(), new Map()];\n  for (const group of groups) {\n    group.lines.forEach((lines, side) => {\n      for (const line of lines) {\n        byLine[side].set(line, group);\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  const anchors = anchorsOf(pairs, counts);\n  return {\n    pairs,\n    groups,\n    anchors,\n    exact: pairs.length > 0,\n    // The group a line belongs to, if any.\n    groupAt: (side, line) => byLine[side].get(line),\n    // The lines [first, last] on the other side of lines [first, last]:\n    // those matched to them, or else those at the same place.\n    mapRange(side, first, last = first) {\n      const other = [];\n      for (const pair of pairs) {\n        if (pair[side] >= first && pair[side] <= last) {\n          other.push(pair[1 - side]);\n        }\n      }\n      if (other.length) {\n        return { lines: [Math.min(...other), Math.max(...other)], exact: true };\n      }\n      const start = Math.floor(mapPosition(anchors, first, side));\n      const end = Math.ceil(mapPosition(anchors, last + 1, side)) - 1;\n      return { lines: [start, Math.max(start, end)], exact: false };\n    },\n    mapPosition: (side, position) => mapPosition(anchors, position, side),\n  };\n}\n"

A phrase that makes no name gives undefined.\nfunction neutralOf(phrase) {\n  const words = nameWords(phrase.replace(/[^\\p{Alphabetic}\\p{N}_\\s]+/gu, ' '));\n  const name = words.join('-');\n  return nameStart.test(name) ? name : undefined;\n}\n\n// Neutral name -> its translation, for the names that change. 0);\n  const next =\n    line < lineCount(editor)\n      ? editor.getTopForLineNumber(line + 1) - editor.getTopForLineNumber(line)\n      : 0;\n  return Math.max(typeof height === 'number' ? height : 0, next, 1);\n}\n\n// The line at the top of an editor, with the fraction of it scrolled past\n// (0-based: 2.5 is half way through the third line).\nexport function topPosition(editor) {\n  const count = lineCount(editor);\n  const scroll = editor.getScrollTop();\n  let low = 1;\n  let high = count;\n  while (low < high) {\n    const middle = (low + high + 1) >> 1;\n    if (editor.getTopForLineNumber(middle) <= scroll) {\n      low = middle;\n    } else {\n      high = middle - 1;\n    }\n  }\n  const top = editor.getTopForLineNumber(low);\n  const fraction = clamp((scroll - top) / lineHeight(editor, low), 0, 1);\n  return low - 1 + fraction;\n}\n\n// Scrolls an editor so that a position (as topPosition gives it) is at\n// its top.\nexport function scrollToPosition(editor, position) {\n  const count = lineCount(editor);\n  if (!count) {\n    return;\n  }\n  const at = clamp(position, 0, count);\n  const line = Math.min(count, Math.floor(at) + 1);\n  const fraction = at - (line - 1);\n  editor.setScrollTop(\n    editor.getTopForLineNumber(line) + fraction * lineHeight(editor, line)\n  );\n}\n\n// The lines [first, last] (0-based) of a selection; a selection that ends\n// at the start of a line does not take that line.\nfunction selectionLines(selection) {\n  const first = selection.startLineNumber - 1;\n  let last = selection.endLineNumber - 1;\n  if (last > first && selection.endColumn === 1) {\n    last -= 1;\n  }\n  return [first, last];\n}\n\n// The folded regions of an editor, by their first line (0-based).\nfunction foldedStarts(regions) {\n  const starts = new Set();\n  for (let index = 0; index < (regions?.length ?? 0); index += 1) {\n    if (regions.isCollapsed(index)) {\n      starts.add(regions.getStartLineNumber(index) - 1);\n    }\n  }\n  return starts;\n}\n\nasync function foldingModel(editor) {\n  try {\n    return (await editor.getContribution(foldingId)?.getFoldingModel()) ?? Library names stay as they are. When the code language stays, the change is made in place, keeping every other character. Each name is spelled in the naming convention of the target (`суммаКвадратов`, `сумма_квадратов`) and transliterated for targets whose names are ASCII only (`summa_kvadratov` in C). The Rust twin is rust/src/meta/library.rs.\n\nimport { node } from './tree.js';\n\nexport const standardLibrary = 'standard';\n\n// Procedure name -> the concept it stands for.\nexport const standardProcedures = {\n  'print-line': {\n    concept: 'Print',\n    parameters: ['value'],\n    fields: { newline: true },\n    statement: true,\n  },\n  print: {\n    concept: 'Print',\n    parameters: ['value'],\n    fields: { newline: false },\n    statement: true,\n  },\n  length: { concept: 'Length', parameters: ['array'], returns: 'integer' },\n};\n\nconst isNode = (value) =>\n  value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value);\n\nfunction mapTree(value, visit) {\n  if (Array.isArray(value)) {\n    return value.map((item) => mapTree(item, visit));\n  }\n  if (!isNode(value)) {\n    return value;\n  }\n  const mapped = Object.fromEntries(\n    Object.entries(value).map(([field, item]) => [field, mapTree(item, visit)])\n  );\n  return value.kind ? visit(mapped) : mapped;\n}\n\nconst libraryCall = (callee, args, rest) =>\n  node('Call', { ...rest, callee, library: standardLibrary, arguments: args });\n\nfunction generalNode(tree) {\n  if (tree.kind === 'Print') {\n    const { kind, value, newline, ...rest } = tree;\n    const callee = newline ? 'print-line' : 'print';\n    return node('Evaluate', {\n      ...rest,\n      expression: libraryCall(callee, [value], {}),\n    });\n  }\n  if (tree.kind === 'Length') {\n    const { kind, array, ...rest } = tree;\n    return libraryCall('length', [array], rest);\n  }\n  return tree;\n}\n\n// The procedure of the standard library a call names, when it takes the\n// arguments the procedure needs.\nfunction procedureOf(call) {\n  if (call?.kind !== 'Call' || call.library !== standardLibrary) {\n    return undefined;\n  }\n  const procedure = standardProcedures[call.callee];\n  return procedure?.parameters.length === (call.arguments ??                 "+// The line number beside the first element `selector` of an editor.",

                "+  return tab.$eval(`${id} ${selector}`, (it) => {",

                "+      it.getBoundingClientRect().top + it.getBoundingClientRect().height / 2;",
                "+    const number = [",

                "+    ].find((line) => {",
                "+      const box = line.getBoundingClientRect();",
                "+      return box.top <= middle && box.bottom >= middle;",
                "+    });",
                "+    return Number(number?.textContent);",
                "+  });",

effect, as a statement.\n    pub statement: bool,\n}\n\n/// The procedures of the standard library.\npub const STANDARD_PROCEDURES: [Procedure; 3] = [\n    Procedure {\n        name: \"print-line\",\n        concept: \"Print\",\n        parameters: &[\"value\"],\n        newline: Some(true),\n        statement: true,\n    },\n    Procedure {\n        name: \"print\",\n        concept: \"Print\",\n &[\"array\"],\n        newline: None,\n        statement: false,\n    },\n];\n\nfn library_call(callee: &str, argument: Option<Value>, mut call: Node) -> Node {\n    call.kind = \"Call\".to_owned();\n    call.set(\"callee\", callee);\n    call.set(\"library\", STANDARD_LIBRARY);\n    call.set(\"arguments\", Value::List(argument.into_iter().collect()));\n    call\n}\n\nfn general_node(mut tree: Node) -> Node {\n    match tree.kind.as_str() {\n        \"Print\" => {\n            let callee = if tree.flag(\"newline\") == Some(true) {\n                \"print-line\"\n            } else {\n (count == procedure.parameters.len()).then_some(procedure)\n}\n\nfn concept(procedure: &Procedure, call: &Node, mut rest: Node) -> Node {\n    rest.kind = procedure.concept.to_owned();\n    let rewrite(tree, special_node)\n}\n"

Helpers (new_array, print_*) carry no `.type`, so the reader only reads `.type` blocks.\n   - Data: `label: .asciz \"...\"` with octal escapes. Formats: integer_format, text_format, newline_format. Texts: text_N.\n   - Comment char `#`. `call printf@PLT`, `call malloc@PLT`, `leaq text_0(%rip), %rdi`. Footer `.section .note.GNU-stack,\"\",@progbits`.\n   - Reader mirrors the nasm reader (pop/push sequences, \"pushq %rax\" after a call as the result marker).\n\n   **arm64 (done in JS writer)**\n   - 16-byte stack cells: push is `str x0, [sp, #-16]!`, pop is `ldr xN, [sp], #16`.\n   - Prologue: `stp x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!`, `sub sp, sp, #frame`, `mov x29, sp`.\n   - Slots: `.set fn.slot, 8*slot`, used as `[x29, #fn.slot]`.\n   - Epilogue always: `mov sp, x29`, `add sp, sp, #frame`, `ldp x29, x30, [sp], #16`, `ret`. main return-nothing is `mov x0, #0` plus the epilogue.\n   - Push: `mov x0, #v` if -65536 to 65535, else `ldr x0, =v`.\n   - Conditions: b.eq, b.ne, b.lt, b.le, b.gt, b.ge. Calls pop into x(n-1)..x0, then `bl name`, and `str x0` pushes the result.\n   - print-text: `adrp x0, text_N`, `add x0, x0, :lo12:text_N`, `bl print_text`.\n   - Arrays: `bl new_array`, `ldr x0, [x0, x1, lsl #3]`, length at `[x0, #-8]`.\n   - Comment `//`. `.type name, %function` ... `.size`.\n   - Not yet checked: that clang accepts `[x29, #sym]` with a `.set` symbol. Parameters are `%name` with prologue stores `store i64 %p, ptr %p.addr`. Entry block named `entry.0`. Temporaries `%t.N`. Blocks named by lowering labels.\n   - Writer uses an abstract stack of entries {value, type, spill index}. Loads, calls and prints are emitted immediately. Constants are deferred.\n   - Operations:\n     - arithmetic: add, sub, mul, sdiv, srem\n     - negate: `sub nsw i64 0, %a`\n     - compare: `icmp eq|ne|slt|sle|sgt|sge`, then `br i1 %c, label %L, label %next.N`, then a `next.N:` block\n     - new-array: `call ptr @new_array(i64, i64)`\n     - element: `getelementptr i64, ptr %arr, i64 %idx`\n     - length: `getelementptr i8, ptr %arr, i64 -8` then load\n     - dup: reuse the same SSA name\n     - element-index: no-op\n   - Prints are `call i32 (ptr, ...) @printf(ptr @integer_format, i64 %v)` and `@printf(ptr @text_format, ptr @text.N)`.\n   - `ret i64 %v`. `ret void`. main is `define i32 @main()` with `ret i32 0`. `unreachable` at the end of non-terminated returning functions. `dead.N:` blocks after terminators.\n   - Stack entries live at a branch or label are spilled to allocas `%stack.N` (ptr entries to `%stack.ptr.N`) before `br` or fallthrough `br`, and reloaded at the label. Redundant spills (an entry that is the reload of the same index) are skipped. Comment `;`.\n   - Reader design:\n     - Line-by-line pass with a map `%t -> pending fragment` and textual use counts.\n     - Pure values (arithmetic, icmp, gep, loads, value calls) are lazy.\n     - Effects are emitted immediately: stores, void calls, printf, br, ret, labels.\n     - A value with use count 0 is emitted followed by `pop`.\n     - A value with use count above 1 is pinned: emitted at definition, `dup` for every use but the last, `[]` for the last.\n     - `store` to `%stack.*` emits the fragment (the value stays on the stack). A `load` from `%stack.*` is the empty fragment.\n     - `br label %X` directly followed by `X:` is dropped. `next.*` and `dead.*` labels are dropped. `unreachable` is ignored. A parameter-prologue store is skipped. `ret i32 0` in main is return-nothing.\n     - A gep with `i8` and -8 is the length pointer; a gep with `i64` is an element pointer.\n\n   **wat (designed, not written)**\n   - Imports `env.print_integer (param i64)`, `env.print_text (param i32 i32)`, `env.print_newline`.\n   - `(memory (export \"memory\") ...)`, data segments `(data (i32.const OFF) \"...\")` with hex escapes, global heap bump pointer, helper `$new_array` (skipped by name in the reader). `(func $main (export \"main\")`.\n   - All values are i64, arrays included (address as i64).\n   - Array access: `i64.const 3 / i64.shl / i64.add / i32.wrap_i64 / i64.load` (store analogous). The reader emits `element-index` plus `load-element` for the read pattern.\n   - Length is read at address minus 8.\n   - Negate is `i64.const -1`, `i64.mul`. dup is `local.tee $.dup` plus `local.get $.dup`. pop is `drop`.\n   - Helper locals are dotted so they cannot clash with identifiers: `$.pc`, `$.dup`, `$.cond`, `$.stack.N`.\n   - Control flow: nested blocks, one per label, named `$L1..$Ln` outermost to innermost.\n     - Without backward jumps there is no loop. The writer emits `block $Ln ... block $L1 <section0> end <section1> end ...`, and a forward jump is `br $Lk`.\n     - With any backward jump (a jump at section j to the label with index k, where k is at most j) it adds `loop $dispatch`, an innermost `block $start`, `local.get $.pc`, `br_table $start $L1 ... $Ln $start`, and `end`.\n       - A backward jump is `i32.const k`, `local.set $.pc`, `br $dispatch`.\n       - A backward conditional jump is `<rel op>`, `if`, `i32.const k`, `local.set $.pc`, `br $dispatch`, `end`.\n   - compare ops: i64.eq, i64.ne, i64.lt_s, i64.le_s, i64.gt_s, i64.ge_s, then `br_if $Lk` (forward).\n   - Return: functions with a result get `unreachable` at the end. `return` maps to return or return-nothing by whether the function has `(result i64)`.\n   - Stack values live across labels or jumps are spilled with `local.set $.stack.N` (top first) and reloaded with `local.get`. For a compare-jump with remaining stack depth above 0, use `local.set $.cond`, spill, reload, `local.get $.cond`.\n   - Reader:\n     - Pre-pass collects function parameter counts.\n     - Drops `local.set/get $.stack.*` and `$.cond` lines as no-ops.\n     - Keeps a block-name stack. On `end`, a popped name other than `start` or `dispatch` emits `label name`.\n     - Forward `br $L` emits a jump. `i32.const k / local.set $.pc / br $dispatch` emits a jump to the k-th br_table target.\n     - `<rel> / br_if $L` emits compare-jump. The backward `if` form also emits compare-jump.\n     - Ignores `unreachable`.\n     - Slot names are the params plus the non-helper locals.\n   - Comment `;;`. A dictionary cannot\n// translate free prose perfectly. Callers with a better translator (a\n// machine translation service, a human) pass it as\n// `translateComment(text, { from, to })`; the dictionary is the default.\n\nimport { naturalLanguage, naturalLanguageIds } from './catalog.js';\nimport { semanticPrimes } from './rules.js';\nimport {\n  grammarOf,\n  knownForm,\n  stemIndex,\n  vocabularyConcepts,\n} from './vocabulary.js';\n\nconst fold = (text) => text.toLocaleLowerCase();\nconst baseOf = (id) => naturalLanguage(id).base ?? id;\n\nlet neutral;\n// Every neutral word some language has a word for.\nfunction neutralWords() {\n  neutral ??= [\n    ...new Set(\n      naturalLanguageIds().flatMap((id) =>\n        Object.keys(naturalLanguage(id).lexicon)\n      )\n    ),\n  ];\n  return neutral;\n}\n\nconst meaningSets = new WeakMap();\n\n// The meanings of one language:\n//   phrases   meaning -> phrases, the preferred phrase first\n//   meanings  phrase -> meanings, the likeliest first\n//   parts     meaning -> part of speech ('prime' and 'name' for the primes\n//             and the words of program names)\nfunction meaningsOf(id) {\n  const language = naturalLanguage(id);\n  if (meaningSets.has(language)) {\n    return meaningSets.get(language);\n  }\n  const base = baseOf(id);\n  const phrases = new Map();\n  const meanings = new Map();\n  const parts = new Map();\n  const add = (meaning, part, phrase) => {\n    if (!phrase) {\n      return;\n    }\n    const folded = fold(phrase);\n    const known = phrases.get(meaning) ?? Prose     { language, sentences }\n//!   Sentence  { words, question? }\n//!   Word      { text, concept? | prime? | word?, part? }\n//!   Code      { language, program }   a quoted piece of code, read\n//! ```\n//!\n//! A word's meaning is a concept of the everyday vocabulary\n//! (data/natural/vocabulary.lino), a semantic prime or a neutral word of\n//! program names, found the way the free translation of prose finds it\n//! (comments.rs): the longest known phrase of up to four words first, an\n//! inflected word through its stem, and in a question the interrogative\n//! meanings first. The JavaScript twin is js/src/natural/prose-reading.js.\n\nuse std::sync::LazyLock;\n\nuse regex::Regex;\n\nuse super::comments::{Meanings, detect_comment_language, fold, likely, meanings_of, pieces};\nuse super::vocabulary::known_form;\nuse crate::meta::tree::{Node, Value};\n\nconst LONGEST_PHRASE: usize = 4;\n/// The longest word looked for inside a text written without spaces.\nconst LONGEST_RUN: usize = 8;\n\nstatic TERMINATORS: LazyLock<Regex> =\n    LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r\"[.!?;。！？؟]\").expect(\"terminators\"));\nstatic QUESTION_MARKS: LazyLock<Regex> =\n    LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r\"[?？؟]\").expect(\"question marks\"));\n\n/// A word and its meaning: `concept:print` -> `(concept print)`.\nfn word(text: &str, meaning: Option<&str>, language: &Meanings) -> Node {\n    let mut node = Node::new(\"Word\").with(\"text\", text);\n    if let Some(meaning) = meaning\n        && let Some((field, value)) = meaning.split_once(':')\n    {\n        node.set(field, value);\n        let part = language.part(meaning);\n        if !part.is_empty() {\n            node.set(\"part\", part);\n        }\n    }\n    node\n}\n\nfn understood(word: &Node) -> bool {\n    !word.is(\"Word\") || word.str(\"part\").is_some()\n}\n\n/// The meaning of a known phrase, through its stem for a single word.\nfn meaning_of(phrase: &str, language: &Meanings, single: bool, question: bool) -> Option<String> {\n    let form = if language.meanings.contains_key(phrase) {\n        Some(phrase.to_owned())\n    } else if single {\n        known_form(phrase, &language.stems, &language.grammar)\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n    form.and_then(|form| likely(&form, language, question).first().map(|it| (*it).clone()))\n}\n\n/// The words of a run of letters written without spaces: the longest known\n/// runs first, unknown letters joined into one word.\nfn segmented(text: &str, language: &Meanings, question: bool) -> Vec<Node> {\n    let letters: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();\n    let mut words: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();\n    let mut at = 0;\n    while at < letters.len() {\n        let found = (1..=LONGEST_RUN.min(letters.len() - at))\n            .rev()\n            .find_map(|size| {\n                let run: String = letters[at..at + size].iter().collect();\n                meaning_of(&fold(&run), language, false, question).map(|meaning| (size, meaning))\n            });\n        if let Some((size, meaning)) = found {\n            let run: String = letters[at..at + size].iter().collect();\n            words.push(word(&run, Some(&meaning), language));\n            at += size;\n            continue;\n        }\n        match words.last_mut() {\n            Some(last) if !understood(last) => {\n                let joined = format!(\"{}{}\", last.str(\"text\").unwrap_or(\"\"), letters[at]);\n                last.set(\"text\", joined);\n            }\n            _ => words.push(word(&letters[at].to_string(), None, language)),\n        }\n        at += 1;\n    }\n    words\n}\n\n/// A word piece of a sentence and the gap before it, or quoted code.\nenum Item<'a> {\n    Word { text: &'a str, gap: &'a str },\n    Code(&'a str),\n}\n\nstruct Sentence<'a> {\n    items: Vec<Item<'a>>,\n    question: bool,\n}\n\n/// The words of one sentence: `run` holds its word pieces and the gaps\n/// between them.\nfn sentence_words(run: &[(&str, &str)], language: &Meanings, question: bool) -> Vec<Node> {\n    let mut words = Vec::new();\n    let mut index = 0;\n    while index < run.len() {\n        let found = (1..=LONGEST_PHRASE).rev().find_map(|size| {\n            let last = index + size - 1;\n            let joined =\n                last < run.len() && run[index + 1..=last].iter().all(|(_, gap)| *gap == \" \");\n            if !joined {\n                return None;\n            }\n            let text = run[index..=last]\n                .iter()\n                .map(|(text, _)| *text)\n                .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n                .join(\" \");\n            meaning_of(&fold(&text), language, size == 1, question)\n                .map(|meaning| (text, meaning, size))\n        });\n        if let Some((text, meaning, size)) = found {\n            words.push(word(&text, Some(&meaning), language));\n            index += size;\n        } else if !language.grammar.spaced {\n            words.extend(segmented(run[index].0, language, question));\n            index += 1;\n        } else {\n            words.push(word(run[index].0, None, language));\n            index += 1;\n        }\n    }\n    words\n}\n\n/// The text cut into sentences: each one a list of word pieces (with the\n/// gap before each word) and quoted code, and whether it asks.\nfn sentences_of(text: &str) -> Vec<Sentence<'_>> {\n    let mut sentences = Vec::new();\n    let mut current = Sentence {\n        items: Vec::new(),\n        question: false,\n    };\n    let mut close = |current: &mut Sentence<'_>, mark: &str| {\n        let done = std::mem::replace(\n            current,\n            Sentence {\n                items: Vec::new(),\n                question: false,\n            },\n        );\n        if !done.items.is_empty() {\n            sentences.push(Sentence {\n                question: QUESTION_MARKS.is_match(mark),\n                ..done\n            });\n        }\n    };\n    for (at, segment) in text.split('`').enumerate() {\n        if at % 2 == 1 {\n            current.items.push(Item::Code(segment));\n            continue;\n        }\n        let mut gap = \"\";\n        for (index, piece) in pieces(segment).into_iter().enumerate() {\n            if index % 2 == 1 {\n                current.items.push(Item::Word { text: piece, gap });\n                continue;\n            }\n            gap = piece;\n            if let Some(mark) = TERMINATORS.find(piece) {\n                close(&mut current, mark.as_str());\n                gap = \"\";\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    close(&mut current, \"\");\n    sentences\n}\n\n/// The words of a sentence, with its quoted code read by `read_code`.\nfn read_sentence(\n    sentence: &Sentence<'_>,\n    language: &Meanings,\n    read_code: &dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<Node>,\n) -> Node {\n    let mut words: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();\n    let mut run: Vec<(&str, &str)> = Vec::new();\n    for item in &sentence.items {\n        match item {\n            Item::Word { text, gap } => run.push((text, gap)),\n            Item::Code(code) => {\n                words.extend(sentence_words(&run, language, sentence.question));\n                run.clear();\n                words.push(read_code(code).unwrap_or_else(|| word(code, None, language)));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    words.extend(sentence_words(&run, language, sentence.question));\n    let node = Node::new(\"Sentence\").with(\n        \"words\",\n        Value::List(words.into_iter().map(Value::Node).collect()),\n    );\n    if sentence.question {\n        node.with(\"question\", true)\n    } else {\n        node\n    }\n}\n\n/// The deep reading of a text as prose of a natural language (the one most\n/// of its words belong to, unless `language` names it), or `None` when no\n/// word of it is known and it quotes no code.\npub fn read_prose(\n    text: &str,\n    language: Option<&str>,\n    read_code: &dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<Node>,\n) -> Option<Node> {\n    let id = language.unwrap_or_else(|| detect_comment_language(&[text]));\n    let meanings = meanings_of(id).ok()?;\n    let sentences: Vec<Node> = sentences_of(text)\n        .iter()\n        .map(|sentence| read_sentence(sentence, &meanings, read_code))\n        .collect();\n    let known = sentences\n        .iter()\n        .any(|sentence| sentence.nodes(\"words\").into_iter().any(understood));\n    known.then(|| {\n        Node::new(\"Prose\").with(\"language\", id).with(\n            \"sentences\",\n            Value::List(sentences.into_iter().map(Value::Node).collect()),\n        )\n    })\n}\n"

crate::natural::prose_reading::read_prose;\nuse crate::natural::words_of;\nuse crate::translator::Translator;\n\n/// The most words a comment or a string keeps in its place.\npub const LONGEST_INLINE_TEXT: usize = 12;\n\nstatic CODE_LIKE: LazyLock<Regex> =\n    LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r\"[(){}\\[\\];=]\").expect(\"code-like characters\"));\n\n/// The field holding the text of a node: a comment's text, a string's value.\nfn text_field(kind: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {\n    match kind {\n        \"Comment\" => Some(\"text\"),\n        \"Text\" => Some(\"value\"),\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\nfn text_of(node: &Node) -> Option<String> {\n    let text = node.str(text_field(&node.kind)?)?;\n    (!text.trim().is_empty()).then(|| text.to_owned())\n}\n\n/// Quoted code is code; a string is code only when it looks like it.\nfn read_code(text: &str, quoted: bool, language: &str, translator: &Translator) -> Option<Node> {\n    if !quoted && !CODE_LIKE.is_match(text) {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let mut candidates = vec![language.to_owned()];\n    for detection in translator.detect_language(text, 3) {\n        if !detection.natural && detection.reads && !candidates.contains(&detection.id) {\n            candidates.push(detection.id);\n        }\n    }\n    candidates.into_iter().find_map(|id| {\n        let fragment = translator.parse_fragment(text, &id).ok()?;\n        Some(\n            Node::new(\"Code\")\n                .with(\"language\", id.as_str())\n                .with(\"program\", fragment.program),\n        )\n    })\n}\n\n/// Read Node::new(\"Paragraph\")\n            .with(\"id\", id.as_str())\n            .with(\"text\", text.as_str())\n            .with_opt(\"reading\", reading(&text, false));\n node.with(\"reference\", id.as_str());\n        }\n        let found = reading(&text, node.is(\"Text\"));\n        node.with_opt(\"reading\", found)\n    });\n    if texts.is_empty() || The others write the counting loop\n// over a fresh index whose body starts by reading the element,\n//\n//   for index in 0..len(a): x = a[index]; ...\n//\n// and the rule that reads a program raises loop everywhere, as the native loop variable is read-only in\n// many languages and the array may not be changed while it is read.\nconst isPlain = (loop) =>\n  !changes(loop.body, loop.variable) && return node('CountingLoop', {\n    variable: index,\n    start: number(0),\n    end: node('Length', { array, type: 'integer' }),\n    body: block([element, ...body.statements]),\n  });\n}\n\n// The others write the counting loop\n// over a fresh index whose body starts by reading the element,\n//\n//   for index in 0..len(a): x = a[index]; ...\n//\n// and the rule that reads a program raises that loop back to a ForEach, so\n// that every language round-trips to the same meta program.\n\nimport { freshName, usedNames } from './arrays.js';\nimport { languageSyntax } from './languages.js';\nimport { block, node, number, rewrite, walk } from '../meta/tree.js';\n\nconst mentions = (tree, identifier) => {\n  let found = false;\n  walk(tree, (current) => {\n    if  current.name === identifier\n    ) {\n      found = true;\n    }\n  });\n  return found;\n};\n\n// A loop that changes its own variable or the array it reads is written as\n// a counting loop Key Technical Concepts:\n   - Dictionary-based \"free translation\" via meanings:\n     - Meaning ids are `prime:*`, `word:*` (the neutral lexicon words of program names, part 'name') and `concept:*` (vocabulary.lino, part per concept).\n     - `likely()` orders meanings by the rank of the phrase in each meaning's phrase list. Ties follow insertion order: primes, then words, then concepts.\n     - `translatePhrase` takes the first meaning the target has.\n     - `preferredPhrase` takes the first target phrase that reads back to that meaning.\n   - Vocabulary convention: per concept `part:` plus per-language forms, most frequent first. For verbs, slot 0 = lemma/infinitive, slot 1 = 3sg present, slot 2 = past (unreliable across rows). Nouns have nominative singular first, then plural and other cases.\n   - Grammar fields: `infinitive`, `verb-lemma`, `endings`, `spaced`. Planned additions: `verb-forms` (slot names, matched by name between source and target), object endings and pronoun forms, and an \"of\" genitive flag.\n   - JS reads data via the generated js/src/natural/sources.js, which must be rebuilt with `node scripts/build-natural-sources.mjs` after any .lino change (CI uses `--check`). Rust embeds the same files through `SOURCES` in catalog.rs.\n   - Rust and JS twins: `Meanings`/`meaningsOf`, `translate_phrase`/`translatePhrase`, `ProseTranslator`, `translate_comment_text`/`translateCommentText`, and `Grammar`/`grammarOf`.\n   - Harness quirk: bash commands that mention \"git\" (even inside words like \"digits\") or are too complex are refused in this worktree-isolated session. Key Technical Concepts:\n   - The meta program is lowered to a stack machine (js/src/formal/lowering.js, rust/src/formal/lowering.rs).\n     - Instruction enum in Rust: Comment(String), Push(f64), Load(usize), Store(usize), Pop, Arithmetic(&'static str), Negate, Label(String), Jump(String), CompareJump(&'static str, String), Call(String, usize), Return, ReturnNothing, PrintInteger, PrintText(String), PrintNewline, NewArray, Dup, ElementIndex, LoadElement, StoreElement, ArrayLength.\n     - `Procedure` has name, parameter_count, slot_count, slot_names, slot_arrays: Vec<bool> (the JS `slotTypes[slot] === 'array'`), returns, max_depth, comments, code.\n     - `LoweredProgram` has comments, functions, main.\n     - Relation names are \"equal\", \"notEqual\", \"less\", \"lessOrEqual\", \"greater\", \"greaterOrEqual\". Arithmetic names are \"add\", \"subtract\", \"multiply\", \"divide\", \"remainder\".\n   - Writers spell this code per target. Readers parse text back into the same stack code, and `liftProgram` (lifting.js/.rs) rebuilds meta.\n   - Golden files `examples/programs/translated/<task>/<task><ext>` (18 tasks) are the JS/Rust parity mechanism. Extensions: nasm .asm, gas .s, arm64 .arm64, cil .il, jvm .j, llvm .ll, wat .wat.\n     - `node examples/programs/write-translations.mjs` generates them; `--check` reports drift (currently clean).\n     - rust/tests/lifting.rs reads them through an `extension()` map (currently nasm \"asm\", cil \"il\", other \"j\"). It needs gas \"s\", arm64 \"arm64\", llvm \"ll\", wat \"wat\".\n   - Comment adaptation uses the target label (\"<Task> in <label>\"). The NASM label change affects rust/tests/grammar.rs ~line 413, which must assert '; Greatest common divisor in x86-64 assembly (NASM)'. Rust tests that count targets (35 becomes 39) must be updated as well.\n   - Rust places still to change:\n     - `MACHINE_TARGETS` in rust/src/formal/languages.rs (~line 1321). It needs the nasm relabel and the 4 new targets: gas (lineComment '#', terms call 'call instruction', routine 'function'); arm64 ('//', call 'branch instruction', routine 'function'); llvm (';', 'call instruction', 'function'); wat (';;', 'call instruction', 'function'). All use naming snake.\n     - Translator listing in rust/src/translator.rs ~448-470 (`languages()`, `LanguageListing`, add a `machine` field).\n     - CLI in rust/src/main.rs ~372.\n     - Rust tests: grammar.rs, lifting.rs, common_library.rs, fragments.rs, issue_6.rs, and others that count or snapshot the listing.\n   - JS writer designs (all verified in JS):\n     - gas: AT&T mirror of NASM. `.set fn.slot, -8*(slot+1)`, used as `fn.slot(%rbp)`; local labels `.L<fn>_<label>`.\n     - arm64: 16-byte stack cells; `.set fn.slot, 8*slot`; used as `[x29, #fn.slot]`.\n     - llvm: allocas `%name.addr`; spills `%stack.N` / `%stack.ptr.N`; temporaries `%t.N`; blocks `entry.0`, `next.N`, `dead.N`; printf-based printing.\n     - wat: details in section 3 under \"machine_wasm.rs to port\".\n\n3. The depth is clamped at 0.\n       - `hasBackwardJump`: the section counter increments on a label; a jump or compare-jump whose target has `labels.indexOf(target)+1 <= section` is backward.\n       - `WatFunction` fields: labels, dispatch, body, depth, spilled (max depth), terminated, section, labelDepths, and helpers (set of '.pc', '.cond', '.dup', '.value').\n       - Methods: `spill(depth)` yields `local.set $.stack.{depth-1-i}`; `reload(depth)` yields `local.get $.stack.i`; `jump`, `compareJump`, `label`, `printText`, `instruction`, `opening`, `declarations`, `write`.\n       - `simple` instruction mapping: push -> `i64.const V`; pop -> drop; negate -> `i64.const -1`, `i64.xor`, `i64.const 1`, `i64.add`; call -> `call $name`; dup -> `local.tee $.dup`, `local.get $.dup`; element-index -> `i64.const 3`, `i64.shl`; load-element -> `i64.add`, `i32.wrap_i64`, `i64.load`; store-element -> `local.set $.value`, `i64.add`, `i32.wrap_i64`, `local.get $.value`, `i64.store`; array-length -> `i64.const 8`, `i64.sub`, `i32.wrap_i64`, `i64.load`.\n       - Special cases: return and return-nothing both emit `return`; print-text emits `i32.const offset`, `i32.const length`, `call $print_text`.\n       - Texts are data segments with offsets assigned cumulatively in UTF-8 byte length (a map by text), and `$heap` starts at ceil(size/8)*8.\n       - Layout: comments, a blank line, `(module`, 3 imports, `(memory (export \"memory\") 256)`, `(data (i32.const off) \"...\")` lines, an optional `(global $heap (mut i32) (i32.const N))`, a blank line, functions separated by blank lines, and an optional blank line plus the `watNewArray` constant (the 43-line array in the JS source). Then `)` and a trailing empty element.\n       - Function format: `(func $name (export \"main\") (param $a i64)... (result i64)`; declarations; `opening` (blocks in reverse label order; with dispatch: `loop $dispatch`, blocks, `block $start`, `local.get $.pc`, `br_table $start $l1.. $start`, `end ;; start`); body; `end ;; dispatch`; `unreachable` when needsEnd (returns && (dispatch || last !== 'return')); `  )`.\n       - Declaration order: non-parameter slot locals, then helpers ('.pc' i32, '.cond' i32, '.dup', '.value' i64), then `$.stack.N` locals.\n     - Still to port: the JS readers (js/src/formal/machine-reader-shared.js, machine-reader-assembly.js, machine-reader-llvm.js, machine-reader-wasm.js) to Rust. When `--comment-from` is left out, the comment language is detected:\n\n```bash\nuniversal-translator translate javascript python@2 app.js --comment-language russian\nuniversal-translator translate python python app.py --comment-language german  # comments only\nuniversal-translator meta python app.py   # the meta language as an indented tree\nuniversal-translator meta python app.py --json   # the same program as JSON\n```\n\nThe meta view is indented Links Notation: one line per node with its kind,\nits main value and its other plain fields as `(name value)` links, and its\nchild nodes nested below it with no field labels and no block markers. A\nfield that follows a block, such as the `else` branch, is introduced by one\nplain word (`otherwise`):\n\n```\nprogram\n  function twice (blank-after true) (return-type integer)\n    parameter n (type integer)\n    if\n      binary greater (type boolean)\n        name n (type integer)\n        number 1 (type integer)\n      return\n        binary multiply (type integer)\n          name n (type integer)\n          number 2 (type integer)\n      otherwise\n        return\n          number 0 (type integer)\n  call print-line (library standard)\n    call twice (type integer)\n      number 3 (type integer)\n```\n\nThe meta view shows a program in its general form. Printing a line and\ntaking the length of an array are no special parts of the meta language:\nthey are calls to procedures of its standard library (`print-line`,\n`print`, `length`), each of which every target spells in its own way\n(`console.log`, `print`, `printf`, `len`, `.length`, ...). `generalize`\nand `specialize` move a meta program between this general form and the\nconcepts the emitters work on, and `fromMeta` accepts either form:\n\n```js\nimport { generalize, specialize } from '@link-foundation/universal-translator';\n\nconst meta = translator.toMeta(\n  'numbers = [1, 2]\\nprint(len(numbers))\\n',\n  'python'\n);\nconst general = generalize(meta);\n// Evaluate { Call print-line (library standard) [Call length (library standard) [numbers]] }\ntranslator.fromMeta(general, 'c'); // printf(\"%d\\n\", (int) (sizeof numbers / sizeof numbers[0]));\nspecialize(general); // the same program as toMeta wrote it\n```\n\n```js\nimport {\n  createTranslator,\n  formatMeta,\n  translateComments,\n  versionsOf,\n  naturalLanguageVersions,\n} from '@link-foundation/universal-translator';\n\nconst translator = createTranslator();\ntranslator.translate('// number\\nlet x = 1;\\n', 'javascript', 'python@2', {\n  commentLanguage: 'russian',\n}); // '# число\\nx = 1\\n'\ntranslateComments('# number\\nx = 1\\n', 'python', { to: 'russian' });\nformatMeta(translator.toMeta('x = 1\\n', 'python'));\nversionsOf('python'); // [{ version: '3', default: true }, { version: '2' }]\nnaturalLanguageVersions('english'); // regions, standards and minimal-english\n```\n\nEvery natural language has a `minimal-<id>` version restricted to the 65\nsemantic primes of Natural Semantic Metalanguage. `createStandard`,\n`defineWord` and `wikidataLookup` build a standard of at most 1024 words\nwhose other words are defined recursively through it. Languages with a for-each syntax write it natively (the `for_each`\n//! template of their description in languages.rs). The others write the\n//! counting loop over a fresh index whose body starts by reading the element,\n//!\n//! ```text\n//!   for index in 0..len(a): x = a[index]; ...\n//! ```\n//!\n//! and the rule current.is(\"Declaration\") || current.is(\"IndexAssignment\"))\n            && current.str(\"name\") == Some(identifier)\n        {\n            found = true;\n        }\n    });\n    found\n}\n\n/// .with(\"name\", variable)\n        .with(\"type\", \"integer\")\n        .with(\n            \"value\",\n            Node::new(\"Index\")\n                .with(\"array\", array.clone())\n the two command lines print the same output                                              | the Rust tests named in each row                                                                 |\n\n### Status\n\nThis section is updated as the work lands. Rows R15, R16, R17, R20 and R23\nare in progress.\n\n## Root Causes\n\nEach problem was reproduced on `main` before the fix. The inputs are in\n`experiments/issue-14/`.\n\n1. **Whitespace is lost (screenshot 1).** The pipeline reads the source to a\n   meta program and prints the target from the meta program alone. The lexer\n   drops spaces, so the emitter can only print its own canonical spacing:\n\n   ```text\n   main:   console.log( \"Hello World!\");  ->  console.log(\"Hello World!\");\n   branch: console.log( \"Hello World!\");  ->  console.log( \"Hello World!\");\n   ```\n\n   This is the classic AST round-trip problem. Roslyn, rowan and LibCST solve\n   it with trivia attached to tokens. Their approach works when source and\n   target share one language and one token stream; a translation changes the\n   tokens. The layout pass (`layout.js`) therefore matches the tokens of the\n   output to those of the source, statement by statement. It then moves the\n   source's spacing, blank lines and comment placement onto the output. It\n   also returns a `lineMap` (output line to source line) that the web app\n   uses for the linked editors.\n\n2. **Comments are not translated (screenshot 2).** Two faults together:\n   - `detectCommentLanguage` scored languages only by the words of the\n     programming templates. «Привет мир» scored 0 everywhere, so it fell back\n     to `english`. With source and target both English, the comment stayed\n     the same.\n   - Even with `--comment-from russian`, the comment dictionary held only\n     the programming vocabulary of each language (`привет` and `мир` are not\n     in it), so no word was replaced:\n\n   ```text\n   main:   // Привет мир  --comment-language english  ->  // Привет мир\n   branch: // Привет мир  --comment-language english  ->  // Hello world\n   ```\n\n   Fix: a shared multilingual vocabulary (`data/natural/vocabulary.lino`,\n   concepts with words in every base language, ranked by frequency) feeds\n   both the detection and the translation of comments.\n\n3. **Auto-detection fails on «Привет» (screenshot 3).** `detectLanguage`\n   counted a natural-language word as evidence only when the language's\n   templates reserve it or its lexicon names it. A greeting is neither, and\n   no template reads it, so every natural language scored 0 and was filtered\n   out:\n\n   ```text\n   main:   detectLanguage('Привет')  ->  []\n   branch: detectLanguage('Привет')  ->  russian (natural) first, score 110\n   ```\n\n4. **«Как хорошо покакать?» fails to translate (screenshot 4).** A natural\n   source had to match a sentence template of an algorithm (`if ... then`,\n   `repeat ...`). Anything else failed with `No sentence template matches`.\n   The issue asks for free translation between natural languages, so a text\n   no template reads is now translated word by word and phrase by phrase\n   through the vocabulary:\n\n   ```text\n   main:   No sentence template matches\n   branch: Detected language: russian / How good to poop?\n   ```\n\n5. **Plain editor by default, no linked view.** The web app defaulted to a\n   textarea with highlight.js colours; Monaco was an option. The two editors\n   shared no state, so there was nothing to keep in sync and no line map to\n   show.\n\n6. **Comments are opaque strings in the meta language.** The meta program\n   kept comments and strings as plain text, so it could not express a code\n   fragment inside a comment or prose inside a string.\n\n7. **`print` is special in the meta language.** Each reader turned\n   `console.log`, `print`, `println!` and the others into a `Print` node, and\n   each emitter printed it. The meta language had no notion of a library\n   function. `meta/library.js` now generalizes such statements to\n   `Call print-line` and specializes them back for the target. The meta\n   notation shows the general form.\n\n## Solutions And Alternatives\n\n- **CST by default.** Alternatives considered (see `prior-art.md` section 1):\n  - a full lossless tree per language, Tree-sitter style. This needs a\n    second grammar for each of more than 30 languages, and does not help\n    across languages;\n  - trivia on meta nodes. This is lost when one statement becomes several.\n\n  The chosen layout pass works on token streams. It needs no grammar changes,\n  and when it cannot match a statement it falls back to the emitter's own\n  formatting.\n- **Linked editors.** Monaco's `onDidScrollChange`,\n  `onDidChangeCursorSelection` and the folding model keep the two editors\n  together through the `lineMap`. Scrolling is mapped block by block, so a\n  block of 3 lines that becomes 7 scrolls proportionally.\n- **Deeper natural language.** The GF approach (an abstract syntax of\n  concepts with one concrete grammar per language) matches the existing\n  meta-language design best. The vocabulary is the abstract lexicon. The\n  prose reader builds `Prose > Sentence > Word` with concept and part of\n  speech; Link Grammar and UD-style dependencies are the next layer\n  (`architecture.md`).\n- **Nested grammars.** These follow Tree-sitter injections: a node of one\n  grammar holds a reading in another. The reading sits next to the text, so\n  emitters that do not know it can ignore it, and `unnest` restores the plain\n  program.\n\n## Debug Output\n\n- `universal-translator translate ... --trace` (JavaScript and Rust) prints\n  the tree after each stage (`[parsed]`, `[understood]`, `[typed]`, the rule\n  layers) to standard error.\n- `universal-translator meta <language> <file>` prints the nested meta\n  program; `--shallow` prints the plain one, and `--json` prints it as JSON.\n- The web app logs editor, folding and mapping events to the console when\n  opened with `?debug` (`examples/universal-app/src/debug.js`).\n"
